programme.title: The Inspire Action Podcast
programme.desc:
What does it mean to be part of nature, not apart from it? And how can an ancient philosophy guide us toward practical, systemic change in the modern world?
In this episode of the Inspire Action Podcast Ciara sits down with Dr. Simon Sadinsky - professor, Executive Director of Education, and in-house Harmony advisor at the Kings Foundation - to explore a philosophy that has guided cultures and peoples around the world for millennia, but is now finally being integrated into Western thought via a few key changemakers along the way. It shouldn’t be revolutionary, but it is in our world where progress often comes at the cost of the natural world around us.
Simon reminds us that Harmony isn't just philosophy - it's a practical roadmap for action. This conversation will hopefully shift how you see your place in the world, and remind you (as it did for us) that we all have a part to play in creating the Harmony our planet so desperately needs.
programme.sub-title: How Can We Reconnect with Nature? with Dr. Simon Sadinsky

programme.title: The Inspire Action Podcast
programme.desc:
What does it mean to be part of nature, not apart from it? And how can an ancient philosophy guide us toward practical, systemic change in the modern world?
In this episode of the Inspire Action Podcast Ciara sits down with Dr. Simon Sadinsky - professor, Executive Director of Education, and in-house Harmony advisor at the Kings Foundation - to explore a philosophy that has guided cultures and peoples around the world for millennia, but is now finally being integrated into Western thought via a few key changemakers along the way. It shouldn’t be revolutionary, but it is in our world where progress often comes at the cost of the natural world around us.
Simon reminds us that Harmony isn't just philosophy - it's a practical roadmap for action. This conversation will hopefully shift how you see your place in the world, and remind you (as it did for us) that we all have a part to play in creating the Harmony our planet so desperately needs.
programme.sub-title: How Can We Reconnect with Nature? with Dr. Simon Sadinsky

If I were in a more wet area, I would have installed a drain, we are in a pretty dry area, and this dirt is mostly granite, clay, and rock. I have found there isn't much settling that occurs in this area.

programme.title: The Inspire Action Podcast
programme.desc:
What does it mean to be part of nature, not apart from it? And how can an ancient philosophy guide us toward practical, systemic change in the modern world?
In this episode of the Inspire Action Podcast Ciara sits down with Dr. Simon Sadinsky - professor, Executive Director of Education, and in-house Harmony advisor at the Kings Foundation - to explore a philosophy that has guided cultures and peoples around the world for millennia, but is now finally being integrated into Western thought via a few key changemakers along the way. It shouldn’t be revolutionary, but it is in our world where progress often comes at the cost of the natural world around us.
Simon reminds us that Harmony isn't just philosophy - it's a practical roadmap for action. This conversation will hopefully shift how you see your place in the world, and remind you (as it did for us) that we all have a part to play in creating the Harmony our planet so desperately needs.
programme.sub-title: How Can We Reconnect with Nature? with Dr. Simon Sadinsky

programme.title: Simple Dwelling

Subtle interventions were made during the heritage renovation, including the inclusion of a glass lift, but all was done to not only honour its past but also reflect how we live today.

programme.title: The Inspire Action Podcast
programme.desc:
What does it mean to be part of nature, not apart from it? And how can an ancient philosophy guide us toward practical, systemic change in the modern world?
In this episode of the Inspire Action Podcast Ciara sits down with Dr. Simon Sadinsky - professor, Executive Director of Education, and in-house Harmony advisor at the Kings Foundation - to explore a philosophy that has guided cultures and peoples around the world for millennia, but is now finally being integrated into Western thought via a few key changemakers along the way. It shouldn’t be revolutionary, but it is in our world where progress often comes at the cost of the natural world around us.
Simon reminds us that Harmony isn't just philosophy - it's a practical roadmap for action. This conversation will hopefully shift how you see your place in the world, and remind you (as it did for us) that we all have a part to play in creating the Harmony our planet so desperately needs.
programme.sub-title: How Can We Reconnect with Nature? with Dr. Simon Sadinsky

programme.title: The Inspire Action Podcast
programme.desc:
What does it mean to be part of nature, not apart from it? And how can an ancient philosophy guide us toward practical, systemic change in the modern world?
In this episode of the Inspire Action Podcast Ciara sits down with Dr. Simon Sadinsky - professor, Executive Director of Education, and in-house Harmony advisor at the Kings Foundation - to explore a philosophy that has guided cultures and peoples around the world for millennia, but is now finally being integrated into Western thought via a few key changemakers along the way. It shouldn’t be revolutionary, but it is in our world where progress often comes at the cost of the natural world around us.
Simon reminds us that Harmony isn't just philosophy - it's a practical roadmap for action. This conversation will hopefully shift how you see your place in the world, and remind you (as it did for us) that we all have a part to play in creating the Harmony our planet so desperately needs.
programme.sub-title: How Can We Reconnect with Nature? with Dr. Simon Sadinsky

programme.title: The Inspire Action Podcast
programme.desc:
What does it mean to be part of nature, not apart from it? And how can an ancient philosophy guide us toward practical, systemic change in the modern world?
In this episode of the Inspire Action Podcast Ciara sits down with Dr. Simon Sadinsky - professor, Executive Director of Education, and in-house Harmony advisor at the Kings Foundation - to explore a philosophy that has guided cultures and peoples around the world for millennia, but is now finally being integrated into Western thought via a few key changemakers along the way. It shouldn’t be revolutionary, but it is in our world where progress often comes at the cost of the natural world around us.
Simon reminds us that Harmony isn't just philosophy - it's a practical roadmap for action. This conversation will hopefully shift how you see your place in the world, and remind you (as it did for us) that we all have a part to play in creating the Harmony our planet so desperately needs.
programme.sub-title: How Can We Reconnect with Nature? with Dr. Simon Sadinsky

programme.desc: Have you ever wondered what it would be like to live in a modern home? A home where the line between inside and out is so blurred that nature sometimes comes crawling into your room. Then take a moment to watch this Desert Wash video and see modern living through a child's eye. It will change your perspective about what site-sensitive modern architecture can be.

programme.title: Simple Dwelling
programme.desc: Sometimes we get a bit stuck in the past with heritage homes, fixating on the original build year and forget that the home and society has evolved over 140 years. Queen Bess Row was built in 1886, and ZGA Studio wanted to keep the heritage alive and relevant but in a more contemporary world. Subtle interventions were made during the heritage renovation, including the inclusion of a glass lift, but all was done to not only honour its past but also reflect how we live today.
programme.sub-title: Keeping the Heritage Alive in this 1880s Home Renovation

programme.title: The Inspire Action Podcast
programme.desc:
What does it mean to be part of nature, not apart from it? And how can an ancient philosophy guide us toward practical, systemic change in the modern world?
In this episode of the Inspire Action Podcast Ciara sits down with Dr. Simon Sadinsky - professor, Executive Director of Education, and in-house Harmony advisor at the Kings Foundation - to explore a philosophy that has guided cultures and peoples around the world for millennia, but is now finally being integrated into Western thought via a few key changemakers along the way. It shouldn’t be revolutionary, but it is in our world where progress often comes at the cost of the natural world around us.
Simon reminds us that Harmony isn't just philosophy - it's a practical roadmap for action. This conversation will hopefully shift how you see your place in the world, and remind you (as it did for us) that we all have a part to play in creating the Harmony our planet so desperately needs.
programme.sub-title: How Can We Reconnect with Nature? with Dr. Simon Sadinsky

programme.title: Simple Dwelling

In this video, we'll show you shipping container homes and building examples from around the world and ask whether or not shipping container construction is the future?
The tiny house movement is growing rapidly and more container buildings are being constructed around the world, but is this the future of sustainable architecture? In this video, we visit a range of shipping container projects, such as Buck Street market and Container City in London, in order to investigate the legibility for growth in the future.
Some people think these buildings are a ‘scam’ while others think they are the future, so let's find out.

programme.title: The Inspire Action Podcast
programme.desc:
What does it mean to be part of nature, not apart from it? And how can an ancient philosophy guide us toward practical, systemic change in the modern world?
In this episode of the Inspire Action Podcast Ciara sits down with Dr. Simon Sadinsky - professor, Executive Director of Education, and in-house Harmony advisor at the Kings Foundation - to explore a philosophy that has guided cultures and peoples around the world for millennia, but is now finally being integrated into Western thought via a few key changemakers along the way. It shouldn’t be revolutionary, but it is in our world where progress often comes at the cost of the natural world around us.
Simon reminds us that Harmony isn't just philosophy - it's a practical roadmap for action. This conversation will hopefully shift how you see your place in the world, and remind you (as it did for us) that we all have a part to play in creating the Harmony our planet so desperately needs.
programme.sub-title: How Can We Reconnect with Nature? with Dr. Simon Sadinsky

If I were in a more wet area, I would have installed a drain, we are in a pretty dry area, and this dirt is mostly granite, clay, and rock. I have found there isn't much settling that occurs in this area.
programme.sub-title: DIY Raised Planter Box from CINDER BLOCKS.mp4

programme.title: Simple Dwelling
programme.desc: On a block measuring only 76m2 (818sqft), it was split in half with a pair of three-bedroom vertical townhouses, which meant they couldn't go 'out', so they went 'up'.
programme.sub-title: This Black Metal Townhouse Design is Inspired by a Handbag

programme.title: Simple Dwelling
programme.desc: Melbourne architect, Jerry Wolveridge of Wolveridge Architects, bought the rural property of his clients, and after a study of local agricultural buildings, decided to design a simple, timber-clad pitched off-grid home. Jerry went a step further, adopting the construction methods of Australian sheds, using steel portal frames and avoiding typical "home" materials.
programme.sub-title: An Architect's Own Family Off-Grid Sustainable Home

programme.title: Austin Flipsters
programme.desc: Susanne and Anthony fully gut this house with plenty of surprises into a modern home you just have to see.

programme.title: Simple Dwelling
programme.desc: Sometimes we get a bit stuck in the past with heritage homes, fixating on the original build year and forget that the home and society has evolved over 140 years. Queen Bess Row was built in 1886, and ZGA Studio wanted to keep the heritage alive and relevant but in a more contemporary world. Subtle interventions were made during the heritage renovation, including the inclusion of a glass lift, but all was done to not only honour its past but also reflect how we live today.
programme.sub-title: Keeping the Heritage Alive in this 1880s Home Renovation

programme.title: Simple Dwelling
programme.desc: Living off the grid in a sustainable, comfortable home is a dream for many, that was certainly the brief that came to Ben Callery Architects. The challenge was to design something that could withstand the elements while embracing all the benefits of off-grid living. It was spectacular getting out to shoot Elemental House and for me, this project is a case study in not just how to live off the grid, but also what makes Australian minimalism.
programme.sub-title: A Home That Epitomises Off-Grid Living

programme.title: Ashley Renne: Sustainable Home
programme.desc: Regrowing scallion from kitchen scraps is one of the easiest DIY zero waste food experiments you can try! Here's how to regrow and harvest your scallions or green onions FAST instead of throwing the scraps away.
programme.sub-title: How To Regrow Scallions From Scraps - Zero Waste Food Tutorial + Harvest

programme.title: Ashley Renne: Sustainable Home
programme.desc: Make sustainable changes to your home with these 7 zero-waste swaps for beginners.

programme.title: Simple Dwelling
programme.desc: The clients were looking for their forever home when they approached Winter Architecture and Field Office Architecture, and they wanted a home that could be intimate for their family of four but also accommodate entertaining large groups of people. With this in mind, the dining area became the central focus, with blockwork to ground the home and timber to provide warmth and softness.
programme.sub-title: A Family's Forever Warm Minimalist Home

programme.title: Simple Dwelling
programme.desc: The need for a new development model is desperately needed, a model which is sustainable and financially accessible with a focus on townhouses in urban locations. Davison Collaborative is that sustainable development model, with ethical developers Liam Wallis and Katya Crema of HIP V. HYPE teaming up with architect Chris Gilbert from Archier to design, build and develop three sustainable townhouses in Brunswick. Oh did we mention they also live here?

programme.title: Ashley Renne: Sustainable Travel
programme.desc: On World Environment Day 2019, history was made -- and Ashley Renne got a chance to be apart of it. The United Airlines "Flight For The Planet" crew flew Ashley and other passengers from Chicago to Los Angeles on the most Eco-Friendly flight in aviation history.
programme.sub-title: Ep 3 - Is This The Most Eco-friendly Flight In History | Biofuel + Zero Waste

programme.title: Ashley Renne: Sustainable Travel
programme.desc: In this first episode, Ashley explores sustainability in Thailand; She arrives in Phuket and takes a speedboat to the Phi Phi Islands where she checks in to Zeavola Resort, a sustainable hotel she found through Green Pearls.
programme.sub-title: Ep 1 - Sustainability In Thailand | Zeavola Resort, Phi Phi Island

programme.title: Desert Architecture
programme.desc: This extraordinary, contemporary southwest home located behind the gates of the secluded community of Eagles Nest in Fountain Hills, Arizona is a luxurious, architectural-masterpiece, has 4 bedrooms, 6 bathroom home, with over 8,200 spacious square feet of custom features such as an elevator, air-conditioned garage with custom roll-up glass garage doors, an RV garage, fire and water features throughout, interior and exterior lit stairs and a custom, modern “cloud ceiling”.

programme.title: Simple Dwelling
programme.desc: Shadow Cottage retains the charm of an existing heritage home while creating something modern and liveable through a sustainable renovation – effectively creating a shadow against the old. I think this sustainable, sensitive house renovation by MRTN Architects showcases what can happen with true collaboration, as we see with the client's Martin and Cheryl May.
programme.sub-title: A Sustainable Addition That Is a ‘Shadow’ of the Original Cottage Home

programme.title: Going Green Architecture & Design
programme.desc:
What will the cities of the future look like? By 2050 the world’s population is expected to reach 9.8 billion and nearly 70 percent of these people are expected to live in urban areas. In this video, we are going to be taking a look at some of the most sustainable cities which are currently under construction. From smart high-tech cities to forest cities we will be taking a closer look at what urban life is going to be like in 2050.
Projects Included are- Liuzhou Forest City. Malaysia Forest City. Dubai Sustainable City. Masdar City, UAE. Self-Sufficient City, Beijing. Oceanix, BIG. New Clark City, Philippines. Amaravati, India. Net City, China.
programme.sub-title: Cities of the Future | The World in 2050

programme.title: Going Green Architecture & Design
programme.desc: Smart building technology is helping save the world. This video will show you how architecture and technology can combine to help save our planet and combat climate change. Featuring- Media TIC, Barcelona. Capita Green, Singapore. Bloomberg HQ, London, and The Edge, Amsterdam.
programme.sub-title: Smart Buildings Saving the World | Visiting Sustainable Architecture

programme.title: Going Green Architecture & Design
programme.desc:
In this video, we'll show you shipping container homes and building examples from around the world and ask whether or not shipping container construction is the future?
The tiny house movement is growing rapidly and more container buildings are being constructed around the world, but is this the future of sustainable architecture? In this video, we visit a range of shipping container projects, such as Buck Street market and Container City in London, in order to investigate the legibility for growth in the future.
Some people think these buildings are a ‘scam’ while others think they are the future, so let's find out.

programme.title: Simple Dwelling
programme.desc: Shadow Cottage retains the charm of an existing heritage home while creating something modern and liveable through a sustainable renovation – effectively creating a shadow against the old. I think this sustainable, sensitive house renovation by MRTN Architects showcases what can happen with true collaboration, as we see with the client's Martin and Cheryl May.
programme.sub-title: A Sustainable Addition That Is a ‘Shadow’ of the Original Cottage Home

programme.title: Hotels ByDesign
programme.desc: Journey through design-forward hospitality at Hotel Kansas City, explore wellness and art at Sensei Lanai, and embrace contemporary coastal elegance at Viceroy Santa Monica.

programme.title: Simple Dwelling
programme.desc: What defines good architecture and ultimately a well-designed home? If there was ever a perfect example it’s One MANI House by Mani Architecture. This home takes a difficult, narrow site and uses it to create an adaptable, flexible, four-bedroom home that is filled with unexpected moments, beautiful design details and lots of natural light. One MANI House brings good architectural principles to life.
programme.sub-title: This Home is The Definition of Good Architecture

programme.title: Desert Architecture
programme.desc: The 5300-square foot home was designed to have the floor plan uniquely configured to provide all the Primary Living spaces at the second level, and all the secondary Bedroom/Bath/Recreation Room at the first level. This floor plan “inversion” provides unbelievable panoramic views that would not have been possible with a conventional floor plan design.

programme.title: Ideas For Your Home
programme.desc: Edison bulbs are a great design element for your home decor, but the challenge with this trend was a lack of energy-efficient bulbs. But now LEDs have advanced to a point where they are not only energy-efficient but beautiful in these new bulb formats.

programme.title: BYOT Backyard Builds
programme.desc: Brent transforms an ordinary backyard shed into a fully equipped home gym—tackling insulation, drywall, flooring, and clever storage to create a functional fitness space.
programme.sub-title: How To Turn A Shed Into A Home Gym

programme.title: Ideas For Your Home
programme.desc: Is your property ready for the winter? We have five tips for you to make sure your landscape and yard are healthy, strong, and ready for next season. We look at everything from mulching leaves, aerating your lawn, over-seeding, fertilizing with organic fertilizers, and creating a warm blanket for shrubs with the leaves that have fallen.

programme.title: Simple Dwelling
programme.desc: The existing 1990s townhouse in South Yarra was quite dark, with an unsuitable layout for today's living. For this home renovation, Winter Architecture approached it by looking at what they can take away and have a more minimalist space that felt clean, white and bright.
programme.sub-title: A Minimalist Home About What You Can Take Away

programme.title: Ideas For Your Home
programme.desc: Home design trends are always changing. But, what is the right choice for your home? Sabine meets with Mahdad Saniee, architect at The Greenwich House to learn about some of the design choices that created such a unique and highly livable home.

programme.title: Desert Architecture
programme.desc: Drawing on the roots of Spanish Colonial homes originally built in the Arcadia Neighborhood this new home sits on ¾ acre lot just south of Camelback Road. The homes three-car garage protrudes out from the main home, forming an intimate courtyard on the front of the home. Noise is buffered from nearby Camelback Road by the mass of the garage. A fireplace provides a focal point to the space.

programme.title: Ideas For Your Home
programme.desc: Your master closet doesn't have to be huge to be functional. The key is well-designed storage solutions that best utilize every inch you have. The storage solutions that Sabine worked into The Greenwich House are no exception. Watch as she takes you through her design choices to create one amazing "his and her" master closet.

programme.title: Bring Your Own Tools
programme.desc: This DIY mobile garage storage tutorial is all about how to build a mobile garge storage system from start to finish. This DIY tote storage solution will free up garage space fast!
programme.sub-title: How To Build Mobile Garage Storage

programme.title: Desert Architecture
programme.desc: This Candelaria Design home, our Tranquil Arizona Ranch, is the personal home for one of our premier builders, John Schultz of Schultz Development, and his lovely wife, Denise. The home is of traditional style but embodies the beauty of Arizona living with a touch of European elegance and detail.
programme.sub-title: Tranquil Arizona Ranch - Paradise Valley, Arizona

programme.title: Simple Dwelling
programme.desc: Taking cues from the relaxed 'beach house' vibe, the home of Topology Studio's Amy Hallett and Darren Kaye took a rundown Victorian and started fresh to create an opportunity to springboard their architecture practice.
programme.sub-title: The Modern Family Beach House of Architect-Duo

programme.title: Desert Architecture
programme.desc: The homeowners love to entertain. Every requirement was about enjoying the Arizona lifestyle while creating a resort-style environment. The architect used materials that are timeless and display well and are lasting. He visited the owners often and every time he did, they are deeply involved in a project such as making a grand meal, and I only see clients enjoying their home.

programme.title: Simple Dwelling
programme.desc: Amanda is an avid art collector and curator, but her Mid-Century home in Ormond was becoming small, and the need for more space for both her art and family was paramount. Foomann Architects were engaged to design a sensitive extension to the Modernist home, originally designed by architect C.C Sainsbury in 1957.
programme.sub-title: This Mid-Century Home Has Been Simply Updated for an Art Lover

programme.title: Simple Dwelling
programme.desc: Architect Douglas Wan wanted something simple for his own tiny apartment, avoiding the fancy gadgetry often found in tiny homes. He thought about how he might want to live in the apartment, with the idea of living a monastic life but in the city.
programme.sub-title: A Minimalist Interior That Gives a Lesson in Tiny Apartment Design

programme.title: America ByDesign: Architecture
programme.desc: America ByDesign: Architecture explores Denver’s Origami House, where Boss Architecture blends bold design with natural surroundings, redefining rural living in an urban setting through innovation and storytelling.

programme.title: Simple Dwelling
programme.desc: Melbourne-based architect Chris Megowan of Megowan Architectural initially designed his apartment for just his wife and himself, however, that changed when they found out they were having twins. What stayed the same was the desire to live and work in the same building, so his architecture practice's office sits below his apartment.
programme.sub-title: An Architect's Mixed-Use Apartment For His Family of Four

programme.title: Landscape Design
programme.desc: Onsite at the first project Landscape Fusion and Chibi Moku made the creative decision to take advantage of a major installation day on the active project in Seminole, FL to showcase the level of coordination and reliance on skilled craftsmanship that is essential to Landscape Fusion’s success as an outdoor living design/build company.
programme.sub-title: Behind the Landscape by Landscape Fusion | Tampa, Florida
